newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: RALLYING-MAKINEN CLOSES IN ON PORTUGAL VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-MAKINEN CLOSES IN ON PORTUGAL VICTORY.

text.p: Reigning world rally champion Tommi Makinen of Finland was poised to seize the lead in this year's title chase as he headed to victory in the Rally of Portugal on Wednesday.

The Mitsubishi driver, who saw his only real rival, Swede Kenneth Eriksson in a Subaru, retire on Tuesday evening, increased his advantage to three minutes and 31 seconds over Belgian Freddy Loix in a Toyota in the first four stages of the final day.
With only five stages left until the finish at Figueira da Foz on Wednesday evening, only a mechanical problem would realistically cost Makinen a debut victory in the Portuguese event.
"The stages have been really good," said Makinen. "Some of them are similar to my home event, the 1000 Lakes Rally, and the car has been no problem at all."
German Armin Schwarz, in a Ford, was poised to move into joint third place in the standings with team-mate Carlos Sainz if he maintains his third position until the end of the rally.

A victory for the Finn would hand him the lead in the world championship following a disappointing start to the season where he has just claimed two third-place finishes from the opening three rounds on the calendar.
The Portuguese event claimed world championship leaders Colin McRae of Britain and Sainz on its opening day.
